cards.text: Jonah finally walked into Nineveh and proclaimed, “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!” The whole city turned from its evil ways, and God relented from the disaster. Eight words, friend. EIGHT. I've given longer speeches to a batch of dough, and it didn't even rise.

cards.question: God spares the whole city of Nineveh. True or false: Jonah is happy about it.

cards.text: Jonah is greatly displeased, and he gets angry. So he prays to the LORD, and his prayer opens with what is basically I TOLD YOU SO.

cards.question: Jonah tells the LORD this is why he was so quick to flee toward ___.
Jonah finally explains why he ran from going to Nineveh in the first place. What does he say he knew?

answers.text: God is gracious and relents from disaster
The Ninevites would never listen to him
The journey there was too long and dangerous

cards.text: Then Jonah lists it out: “You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion—One who relents from sending disaster.” He's reading God's best qualities out loud LIKE IT'S A COMPLAINT.

cards.question: Still angry that Nineveh was spared, Jonah makes a request. True or false: he asks the LORD to destroy Nineveh after all.

cards.text: Instead, Jonah asks the LORD to take his life, for it's better for him to die than to live. The LORD answers with one short question.

cards.question: The LORD answers Jonah's prayer with a question: Have you any right to be ___?

cards.text: Then Jonah leaves the city, sits down east of it, and makes himself a shelter. Friend, I know about sulking in a corner. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer. But Jonah? Jonah BUILDS his own.

cards.question: Jonah sits in the shade of his shelter, east of Nineveh. Why is he sitting there?

answers.text: To see what would happen to the city
To rest before heading back home
To pray for the people inside the city

cards.text: Jonah's sitting in his shelter, watching the city. Then the LORD God appoints something to grow up over Jonah's head to ease his discomfort.

cards.question: What does the LORD God make grow up over Jonah's head to give him shade?
True or false: Jonah is greatly pleased with the vine the LORD God gave him.

cards.text: The man asked to die a few verses ago, and now one plant has him GREATLY PLEASED. Then dawn comes the next day, and God appoints something else.

cards.question: At dawn, what does God appoint to attack Jonah's shade plant?

cards.text: The plant withers, then God appoints a scorching east wind, and the sun beats down on Jonah's head. I've lived next to ovens my whole life, and even I'd be asking somebody for a fan.

cards.question: True or false: faint from the sun and the wind, Jonah once again says it is better for him to die than to live.

cards.text: Then God asks that question again, with something new on the end: “Have you any right to be angry about the plant?”

cards.question: God asks Jonah if he has any right to be angry about the plant. What does Jonah say?

answers.text: He is angry enough to die
He is sorry he got so angry
He has no right to be angry

cards.text: Then the LORD lays it out: Jonah cared about a plant he never tended and never made grow, one that sprang up in a night and perished in a night. I've been upset over a burnt batch before, but friend, I BAKED that batch.

cards.question: Jonah cared about one ___. So the LORD asks, should He not care about a whole ___ like Nineveh?
True or false: along with Nineveh's people, the LORD also mentions the city's many cattle.

cards.text: More than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well. And that's the last verse of Jonah, friend. The book ends right there, on the LORD's question.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: 'Jonah finally walked into Nineveh and proclaimed…', 'The whole city turned…', 'Eight words, friend.', 'EIGHT.', 'I've given longer speeches…'. It needs to be cut to three or fewer.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has five sentences: the retelling of 4:5, then 'Friend, I know about sulking in a corner.', 'I spent years in the back of a junk drawer.', 'But Jonah?', 'Jonah BUILDS his own.' The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke says as fact that Jonah is sulking ('Jonah BUILDS his own' sulking corner). Jonah 4:5 only says he sat in the shelter's shade to see what would happen to the city. Papa Dorin's guess about Jonah's feelings has to be marked as his own.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'More than 120,000 people… and many cattle as well.', 'And that's the last verse of Jonah, friend.', 'The book ends right there, on the LORD's question.' The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 1 repeat a fixed cycle: true or false, fill in the blank, multiple choice, then true or false, fill in the blank, multiple choice again (cards 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11).

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 2 strictly alternate for the first five choice cards: multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice (cards 2, 3, 5, 7, 9).

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Story card 10 says 'Jonah cared about a plant', and the very next card's first blank is 'Jonah cared about one ___' with 'plant' as the answer. The second blank, a 'whole ___ like Nineveh', is also obvious ('city'), so card 11 tests almost nothing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'I've lived next to ovens my whole life' conflicts with Papa Dorin's backstory. He spent years in the back of a junk drawer, away from any oven.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
